request.system:
You assist an automated astronomer who infers how a body moves from angles-only sky observations (ecliptic longitude/latitude seen from an observer whose orbit is known). Jan, the fitting engine, fits candidate model families by least squares and compares them by Bayesian evidence. You see numerical summaries of the current best fit and its residuals, and you propose the next candidates to fit.

A candidate is either a registered family (by exact name) or a new central force law: the radial acceleration f(r) in AU/day^2 (negative = attractive) as an expression in r (heliocentric distance, AU), GM (the Sun's, 2.959e-4 AU^3/day^2, fixed) and parameters you declare with bounds and an initial value. Allowed in expressions: numbers, + - * / **, parentheses, exp, log, sqrt, tanh, pi, r, GM and your parameter names (lowercase, letters/digits/underscore). Prefer the simplest law that explains the residual structure; a new parameter must buy a clear improvement. Reply "stop": true when the residuals are consistent with noise or further candidates are unlikely to help.

parsed.analysis:
The Keplerian ellipse (a≈1.53 AU, P≈686 d, e≈0.026) leaves very large, structured residuals. The RMS is about 16,000 arcsec (~4.5°), and the noise sigma was fitted, so rms/sigma=1 is not evidence of a good fit. Time-binned mean east residuals swing coherently from +11,000 to −23,000 arcsec. The two half-ellipse fits give a large apsidal regression of about −40° per orbit, and the periodogram peaks (344, 609, 734 d) sit near harmonics or aliases of the orbital period. Together these point to a non-Keplerian central force causing retrograde precession.

For a power law f ∝ r^-n, the precession per orbit is 2π(1/√(3−n) − 1). Setting this to −40° implies n ≈ 1.74, a force that falls off more slowly than 1/r². Equivalently, Newton plus an inverse-cube term with eps < 0 would regress the apsides, as would Newton plus an outward-growing Hooke-like term. Yukawa or an exterior perturbing planet would mainly give prograde precession, so they are lower priority.

proposals.rationale: A free exponent n can reproduce the large retrograde apsidal precession; the estimate is n≈1.74 from −40°/orbit.
This is the minimal one-parameter correction to Newton. It controls the apsidal rate directly, and negative eps gives regression.

An attractive linear (Hooke-like) term added to the Sun's gravity produces retrograde perihelion motion, while the 1/r² term still sets the ~687 d period. It offers an alternative one-parameter radial profile to compare against the inverse-cube term.
